title: Arrival
content: The ferry arrived beneath a sky the color of old silver. Mara stood alone at the rail while the island gathered shape ahead: a low harbor, a scatter of lamps, and the archive rising above both.
No birds followed the boat into the bay. The captain noticed her looking and said that the island had always been quiet. He offered no explanation, and she decided not to ask for one.
At the quay, a brass automaton waited with her name written on a narrow slate. Its lantern eyes brightened when she stepped ashore, then it turned and began the climb without a word.
The path wound through empty gardens. Pale flowers leaned toward the automaton as it passed. Behind her, the ferry sounded its horn once and withdrew into the mist.
The archive doors stood open. Warm light crossed the steps, though Mara could see no lamps within. She paused beneath the carved stone lintel and listened to the building breathe.
Inside, shelves rose farther than the light could reach. Ladders moved slowly along their rails with no hands to guide them. Somewhere in the distance, a page turned.
A sealed envelope rested on the reception desk. Her instructions were written inside: catalog the eastern wing, answer no bells after midnight.
Mara read the final sentence twice. Then, from deep inside the archive, a bell rang once. The clock above the desk had stopped at eleven fifty-nine.
